title: A Debt for the Contact
premise: Gideon Dunmore, a disgraced intelligence analyst, receives a calendar invite from a handler who died three days earlier — and when he arrives at the meeting, he finds himself standing over the assassin's latest victim with the killer still in the room. The dead handler left behind a ledger proving a trilateral cover-up that sacrificed an entire field network to protect an arms deal, and Gideon is the only person alive who can authenticate it. Hunted by the assassin tasked with erasing every witness, he assembles a ragtag team of fellow castoffs who become the family he never had. In the end Gideon trades his own freedom — surrendering himself to be discredited one final time — to get the ledger into public hands, while his found family carries the truth forward without him.
about_author: A. M. Ravensworth spent a decade in policy research before turning to fiction, writing thrillers about institutions that fail the people inside them. Ravensworth lives quietly off-grid and refuses all interviews.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Broke and blacklisted after three agency dismissals, Gideon takes anonymous cleanup work. A calendar invite arrives from Handler Elias Voss — dead since Tuesday — scheduling a meeting for tomorrow at 9 p.m. The emotional beat: dread sharpened by curiosity; Gideon has nothing left to lose but goes anyway.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. He arrives at a derelict ferry terminal and finds Voss's body staged like an exhibit, a second man in the shadows — the assassin, watching him. Gideon escapes through the terminal's flooded lower deck with a burner phone Voss left taped under a bench. Beat: terror fused with purpose.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Sent
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. The phone contains fragments of an encrypted ledger: names of a burned field network across three countries, all killed within one week. Gideon recognizes the operational signature — it matches work he was fired for flagging years ago. Beat: vindication curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Counts Corpses
chapters.summary: POV Mara Quist, forensic accountant and fellow exile. She's been tracking money trails that vanish into the same black budget. Gideon approaches her; she nearly shoots him, then shows him her own file of the dead. Beat: two loners recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. They reconstruct the deal: weapons routed through a joint task force, the field network eliminated once they became liabilities. Each government blames the others. Beat: cold clarity about the scale of what they're facing.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Contract
chapters.summary: POV Sable, the assassin. Trained, methodical, contracted to erase everyone connected to Voss's ledger. But the contract specifies Gideon must die publicly, framed — someone wants a scapegoat, not just silence. Beat: professional unease at an order that doesn't fit.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: POV Mara. She brings Gideon to a safehouse run by Tomas Reyes, an ex-communications tech who faked his death years ago. Tomas, paranoid and brilliant, becomes their third member. Beat: fragile trust being built brick by brick.

chapters.title: Frame Job
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. News breaks: Gideon Dunmore wanted for Voss's murder. His old agencies leak just enough to bury him. Beat: betrayal — the institutions that discarded him now weaponize his name.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Key
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Deciphering Voss's encryption requires a cipher key held by Odile Ferrant, a retired cryptographer living under protection in Lisbon. Beat: hope with a price tag attached.

chapters.title: Lisbon Rain
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Extraction attempt in Lisbon goes wrong; Sable intercepts them but hesitates when she sees Odile is civilian. Gideon talks instead of fights — first crack in the hunter's certainty. Beat: unexpected mercy.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: POV Odile. She agrees to decrypt the ledger only if they also expose the death of her son, one of the burned field agents. Her grief reframes the mission: not survival, justice. Beat: mourning converted to resolve.

chapters.title: Decryption Night
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. All-night decryption session; the ledger opens fully — transaction records, kill orders, signatures from officials in all three governments. Beat: triumph immediately shadowed by the knowledge of what possessing this means.

chapters.title: Sable's Doubt
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Reviewing the target list, she realizes her employers intend to burn her too once the job closes. She photographs the contract and doesn't report the Lisbon failure. Beat: the first self-serving lie to her handlers.

chapters.title: The Trap in Rotterdam
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. A supposed journalist offering publication turns out to be bait; the team barely escapes a coordinated raid. Someone inside their circle leaked. Beat: paranoia fracturing the found family.

chapters.title: Accusations
chapters.summary: POV Mara. She confronts Tomas; he confesses he contacted an old contact for help and was traced. Near-collapse of the group, then Gideon chooses forgiveness over exile. Beat: the family holds — barely.

chapters.title: The Broker
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Following the money, they identify the broker who engineered the deal: Cassian Wray, a private intermediary untouchable by any single government. Beat: understanding that the enemy is a system, not a man.

chapters.title: Sable Makes Contact
chapters.summary: POV Sable. She approaches Gideon alone, unarmed, offering her contract files in exchange for inclusion in the exposure. Mara objects violently. Beat: distrust versus necessity.

chapters.title: Terms of Alliance
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Negotiation scene; Gideon accepts Sable's terms because her files prove Wray ordered the framing. The team expands to five. Beat: uneasy coalition forged from enemies.

chapters.title: Wray Moves First
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Wray's people hit the safehouse early; Tomas is wounded covering the escape. They lose equipment and half the decrypted copies. Beat: cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Hospital Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Hiding Tomas in a clinic, Mara confronts her own past — she once audited for Wray's network unknowingly. Guilt drives her deeper into commitment. Beat: redemption sought through risk.

chapters.title: The Archive Gambit
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Plan formed: simultaneous release to press outlets in all three countries so no single government can suppress it. They need forty-eight hours and one untraceable broadcast window. Beat: strategy as hope.

chapters.title: Tomas's Tower
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. From a hospital bed, Tomas builds the broadcast rig remotely, guiding them through hijacking a decommissioned relay station. Beat: the wounded man becoming the mission's spine.

chapters.title: Sable's Report
chapters.summary: POV Sable. She feeds her handlers false confirmation of Gideon's death to buy time — a lie that will end her career or her life if discovered. Beat: point of no return crossed.

chapters.title: Wray's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Wray reaches out directly: full pardon, restored reputation, money — if Gideon hands over the ledger and lets the dead stay dead. Beat: temptation aimed at Gideon's deepest wound, wanting to matter again.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Gideon declines, telling Wray the dead already gave him everything he needs. The team watches him choose them over rehabilitation. Beat: the found family solidifying around a shared refusal.

chapters.title: Betrayal Signal
chapters.summary: POV Mara. A tracker hidden in Sable's recovered gear leads Wray's men to their staging site. Sable swears she didn't plant it — and evidence suggests she didn't. Someone else is hunting them. Beat: new threat, old fear.

chapters.title: The Second Hunter
chapters.summary: POV Sable. She identifies the tracker's signature: a rival contractor hired by one government faction that wants the scandal contained differently. Three-way hunt begins. Beat: escalation beyond anyone's control.

chapters.title: Running the Corridor
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Chase sequence through border country; the team splits to draw off both hunters, reuniting at the relay station approach. Beat: endurance, loyalty tested by exhaustion.

chapters.title: Relay Station Dawn
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. They seize the station at dawn. Forty minutes until the broadcast window. Wray's forces and the rival contractor converge. Beat: breathless setup for climax.

chapters.title: Siege
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Holding action at the station; Mara wounded shielding Odile, Sable fighting beside former targets. Beat: sacrifice proving the family real.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. With ninety seconds left, the uplink fails. Gideon transmits the ledger manually, reading key entries aloud on open frequency as soldiers breach the door. Beat: defiant truth-telling at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Captured, Gideon surrenders deliberately so the team can escape with backup copies. He trusts the broadcast worked. Beat: chosen sacrifice.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. In custody, Gideon refuses to recant, forcing interrogators to confront aired evidence. News spreads globally; denials collapse one by one. Beat: quiet strength against institutional pressure.

chapters.title: The World Reacts
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Protests, resignations, parliamentary inquiries. Wray's network unravels as allies scatter. Mara works the press from hiding. Beat: vindication arriving in increments.

chapters.title: Sable's Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Sable. She delivers her contract files to investigators, accepting prosecution for past kills as part of testimony. Beat: accountability embraced freely.

chapters.title: Wray's Fall
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. From detention, Gideon watches Wray arrested after a client state extradites him. The system devours its own servant. Beat: cold satisfaction, no joy.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Gideon's own hearing: charges dropped, reputation partially restored — and an offer to return to service. Beat: the old life extended like a trap.

chapters.title: Turning It Down
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Gideon declines reinstatement, choosing independence with his found family. Odile's son is publicly named among the honored dead. Beat: wholeness found outside the institution.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The team gathers at Tomas's rebuilt safehouse — scarred, diminished, alive. They take on a new case together, unofficially. Beat: warmth, continuity, home.

chapters.title: A Debt Repaid
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Final scene: Gideon visits Voss's grave, leaving the burner phone on the stone. The debt to the dead handler is paid — not with vengeance, but with truth delivered. Beat: closure and quiet peace.
